text: Scythia was a legendary homeland in Irish origin tales. Several early Irish texts, most notably the Book of Invasions, claimed that the Irish people came from Scythia. No ancient country with that exact name ever existed. A nomadic people who lived in eastern Europe were called the Scythians. They were known for horse riding and for lavish goldwork. These Scythians may have met the early Celts in central Europe. The swirl patterns of La Tène art resemble some Scythian designs. The poet Edmund Spenser used this link for a harsh argument. He claimed that the Irish were Scythian barbarians. English settlers could then take their land without moral restraint.

okr.objective: Document Scythia as a legendary origin site in Irish tradition.
